name: scheduling
deprecation_criterion: Superseded when scheduling moves to a different clock source (e.g. a native plugin cron API) or when the tick interval/route become config-driven and this slice's hardcoding is removed.
spec_change_reason: §3.3.3 /tick single tick + /start owns the drain-loop (SKILL-prose only). /auto-maintainer:tick now runs EXACTLY ONE tick (one route pass through any agent-state pause/dispatch/resume) and STOPS at the terminal: a refire final signal is REPORTED (actionable work remains) but the executor does NOT auto-loop into another tick — one /tick = one tick even when the issue pool is not drained. The drain-loop moved to /auto-maintainer:start, which now OWNS it: tick #1 AND each recurring heartbeat, when a completed tick's final signal is refire, fire /auto-maintainer:tick AGAIN immediately, repeating until a non-refire signal (idle/halt/break), so /start drains the backlog promptly; the heartbeat's PROMPT was changed from the single-tick 'Run one auto-maintainer tick now' to the same drain-loop prompt. Both SKILLs edited via the skill-creator workflow: ship/skills/tick/SKILL.md v0.6.0->0.7.0 (frontmatter description, intro, the --step-once note, step 2 done-handling, and the Rules refire bullet); ship/skills/start/SKILL.md v0.3.0->0.4.0 (description, a drain-loop-ownership section, step 2 drain-on-refire, step 4 heartbeat prompt, and a Rules bullet). run_tick.py + its --step/--resume CLI (one tick per --step) and EXIT's POOL-based refire emission are UNCHANGED. Flipped test_refire_e2e behaviour-4 assertions (single-tick/no-auto-loop for /tick; drain-loop ownership + drain-loop heartbeat prompt for /start), bumped the version assertions in test_ship_tick_skill_e2e, and re-anchored the housekeep doc baseline spec.md 1209->1232 for the pre-committed spec growth. Prior reason: Richer + prettier /auto-maintainer:status while staying machine-first. status.py now exposes a machine-first status_data() -> dict of every surfaced field (plugin_version, disposition, awaiting, mode, budget{spent/ceiling/window/paused}, the four read-product counts, reported{filed/skipped}, route{source,states,chain}, runtime_dir) and a DERIVED render_status(data) human view (philosophy §1: the pretty view is produced FROM the machine artifact) with a version-emphasizing header, aligned label/value block, and a Route section rendering the happy-path chain A -> B -> C (shown even when default; no emojis, rule/arrow chars only). The CLI default prints render_status, --json prints status_data() JSON, --line prints the retained byte-identical legacy status_line(). plugin_version is read from <lib_dir>/../.claude-plugin/plugin.json (null when absent). The active route is resolved via two ADDITIVE, side-effect-free run_tick helpers so status never diverges from the loop: resolved_route(project_dir) (shipped default-config/route.json fresh else embedded DEFAULT_ROUTE, then the project-local override via aw.load_route, WITHOUT running/mutating a tick) and the pure route_happy_chain(route_dict). status stays non-mutating (never creates the runtime dir); status_line() is unchanged; run_tick's existing behaviour is unchanged. Added e2e test test_status_pretty_e2e.py; re-anchored the housekeep doc baseline spec.md 1183->1209 for the pre-committed spec growth (scheduling-scope test fixture). Prior reason: Issue-filter wiring — PULL honors issue_filter. make_pull(runtime) now ALSO threads safety-governance's issue_filter into work-intake's Pull, mirroring the existing work_own_filings threading: wi.Pull(source=source, work_own_filings=sg.work_own_filings(gov), issue_filter=sg.issue_filter(gov)). sg.issue_filter is the pure normalizer returning the canonical {labels: List[List[str]], title_pattern: str|None} (no-filter default when absent, so PULL pulls every open issue — non-breaking); a configured filter narrows by DNF labels + title_pattern (work-intake's filtering logic, consumed unchanged). The edit lives ONLY in make_pull; safety-governance and work-intake source are unedited. Added e2e test test_pull_issue_filter_e2e.py; because work-intake's committed contract now calls source(repo, issue_filter=...), the scheduling test stub issue-sources were updated to accept issue_filter=None and the housekeep doc-length baseline re-anchored 1169->1183 (both scheduling-scope test files). Prior reason: Remove the self-deploy ACTION; keep the release_needed DETECTION (the auto-maintainer is NOT self-deployable). run_tick no longer regenerates / commits / pushes the plugin tree: REMOVED _flush_package, git_commit_sink + DEFAULT_PACKAGE_COMMIT_SINK, git_sync_sink + DEFAULT_PACKAGE_SYNC_SINK (#312/#313/#320/#321), the terminal _flush_package call + its results, the package_commit_sink/package_sync_sink run_tick params, the sg.self_deploy gate reference, the self_deployed/deployed_version/deploy_skip_reason trace+event fields, the deploy= trace token, and the bp.bump_version / bp.package_commit_paths references. KEPT the release_needed DETECTION (the human-release-owed operator signal, #319), but SIMPLIFIED _release_needed: dropped the package_deployed param (nothing deploys now) so release_needed = _self_deploy_repo_root(project_dir) resolves AND >=1 merged PR's diff touches shipped src (bp.touches_shipped_src). KEPT gh_pr_files_source + DEFAULT_PR_FILES_SOURCE, _self_deploy_repo_root (own-checkout detector via bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER), the bp import used ONLY for bp.touches_shipped_src + bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER, the terminal _release_needed call, and the release_needed trace token (now standalone) + tick_end event field. Unrelated gh_pr_state_source/pr_state_source (acted-ledger re-entry), REPORT, and refire are untouched. safety-governance (the now-dead self_deploy knob, removed in a follow-up) and packaging-config (KEEP using bp.touches_shipped_src + bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER; bump_version/package_commit_paths removed in a follow-up) are NOT edited. Prior reason: File-referenced dispatch prompt (prompt_path) — deliver each agent-state dispatch's rendered invocation envelope by FILE REFERENCE instead of inline in the --step/--resume stdout JSON, symmetric with the already-file-based subagent OUTPUT, so the executor (orchestrator) never reads or holds the large rendered envelope. The pause previously emitted dispatches[].prompt (ad.render(env)) INLINE in --step stdout; for a large envelope (an IMPLEMENT dispatch with the work-order body + comments) the Bash stdout was truncated, forcing the orchestrator to re-read the whole output to relay the prompt verbatim — pulling the entire envelope into its context. Fix (edits ONLY in run_tick.py + ship/skills/tick/SKILL.md + docs/tests): _pause_result WRITES ad.render(env) to a deterministic ABSOLUTE file under output_dir, named parallel to output_path ('<state>-<di>-<ii>.json' -> '<state>-<di>-<ii>.prompt.md'), sets rec['prompt_path'], and DROPS the inline prompt; the file is written at the PAUSE (where stale OUTPUT files are cleared) and overwritten each emit, so a crash-safety re-emit reproduces the SAME prompt_path with byte-identical content (rendered from the durable checkpoint round-trip, like output_path). The --step/--resume JSON dispatch entries carry prompt_path (a small absolute path) and NOT the multi-KB inline prompt, so stdout stays small (no truncation); subagent_type/description/isolation/output_path/writes/cardinality/item unchanged. The tick executor skill (v0.6.0) dispatches Agent(subagent_type, description, prompt=<a SHORT reference to entry.prompt_path telling the subagent to read its envelope file IN FULL and follow it literally>, isolation?); the orchestrator does NOT open/read prompt_path — the SUBAGENT reads it. Envelope CONTENT is unchanged — only its delivery (file vs inline) changes; agent_dispatch.render and the subagent agent .md files are untouched; the one-step/resume rules, refire loop, and spend metering are unchanged. agent-dispatch / adapter-wiring / verify-integrate / work-intake / safety-governance consumed UNCHANGED. Prior reason: Refire on ANY workable issue in the pool + surface INTEGRATE merge results and the refire decision (two dogfood fixes). (1) REFIRE POOL-BASED: _work_remains is redefined to _work_remains(work_items, triage_memory, backoff_ledger, threshold, now); it computes candidates = _filter_triage_work_items(work_items, triage_memory) (the existing §3.5.3 skip-filter dropping done/deferred-unchanged) and returns True iff any candidate is classify-acceptable (wi.Triage(now).classify=='accepted') AND not blocked-and-unchanged (backoff blocked_count<threshold OR updated_at strictly after deferred_at_updated_at). make_exit is reworked: when tick_outcome=='empty' AND has_acting_agent (gate KEPT so the read-and-idle default still idles) AND _work_remains(...), it rewrites tick_outcome to 'work-remains'. The old committed-work (un-acted/un-handled work_order) gating is REMOVED — the owner's route has no PRIORITIZE so that gate could essentially never fire. make_exit loads triage_memory + backoff from state_path=ctx.read('state_path'); EXIT's manifest stays reads [tick_outcome, work_items, state_path], writes [tick_outcome]. (2) OBSERVABILITY: the tick_end event detail gains merged (count), integrate_skipped (count), integrate_errored (count), merged_refs (list of merged pr_refs) from integration_result, plus refire:true/false; the one-line trace gains a merged=<n> token (and integrate_errored=<n> when >0). All existing detail keys preserved. lifecycle-dispositions, verify-integrate, work-intake, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Immediate-refire when actionable work remains (owner-requested, DESIGN §3.3.3). The loop should run the NEXT tick IMMEDIATELY when actionable work remains, instead of waiting the heartbeat interval. Adds a pure predicate _work_remains(work_items, backoff_ledger, threshold, now) -> True when ANY work_item is BOTH TRIAGE-acceptable (wi.Triage(now).classify(item)[0]=='accepted') AND not blocked-and-unchanged (NOT (backoff[id].blocked_count>=threshold AND item.updated_at NOT strictly after entry.deferred_at_updated_at)); invalid/closed/stale items never count, and a blocked item updated past the pin IS actionable. make_exit now WRAPS lifecycle-dispositions' Exit: when the inner outcome is 'empty' AND the route has an ACTING agent-state (a dispatch entry carrying a truthy effect, threaded onto the runtime dict as has_acting_agent) AND _work_remains over the REMAINING work (this tick's work_items MINUS items already in the durable acted-ledger MINUS items the doer reported `blocked` this tick), it rewrites tick_outcome to 'work-remains' so EXIT emits refire (RUNNING); it overrides ONLY the 'empty' outcome (restart/fault delegated unchanged). EXIT's manifest now reads [tick_outcome, work_items, state_path], writes [tick_outcome], and emits the inner refire/idle/break/halt; work_items is added to the data-readiness initial set. The read-and-idle DEFAULT route + any empty-pool tick still IDLE (back-compat): with no acting agent-state the override never fires. The tick executor skill documents the refire-loop: a 'refire' final signal runs ANOTHER tick immediately, looping until a non-refire signal (idle/halt/break); cron remains the safety net. lifecycle-dispositions, work-intake, durable-state, verify-integrate, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Advisory REVIEW must ALWAYS flow to INTEGRATE (dogfood unmerged-PR root-cause fix). REVIEW became ADVISORY in the loop redesign (it files findings as issues, it is NOT a merge gate) but its AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES['REVIEW']['signal_rule'] was still 'nonempty_else_empty' (gate-era leftover): a clean PR yields ZERO review_findings -> the rule emits EMPTY -> a route edge REVIEW--EMPTY-->PERSIST SKIPS INTEGRATE, so integration_result stays empty every tick and mergeable PRs are never merged. Fix: set AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES['REVIEW']['signal_rule'] to 'always_ok' (the rule already exists in agent_dispatch.compute_signal and returns OK), and flip make_review's deterministic no-op _run to emit 'OK' (was 'EMPTY') while still writing review_findings []. So a zero-finding review emits OK and continues to INTEGRATE. REVIEW's declared emits stay [OK, EMPTY] (verify-integrate REVIEW_MANIFEST UNCHANGED) so seeded routes carrying a REVIEW--EMPTY-->PERSIST edge keep passing validate_signals — the EMPTY edge becomes valid-but-dead (no route.json change). migrate_known_port_entries re-derives a stale REVIEW entry from the template, so a healed entry carries signal_rule='always_ok' automatically. verify-integrate, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Stale/incompatible tick-checkpoint discard-and-fresh (third dogfood crash root-cause fix). The adapter-map migration self-heals the live CONFIG, but a durable tick_checkpoint paused at an agent-state under an OLDER wiring bypasses it: its pending.writes names a slot the current (migrated, seeded) wiring no longer registers (e.g. a v0.7.0 checkpoint paused at REVIEW writing the retired review_verdicts slot). run_tick re-emitted the stale dispatch on --step and applied the subagent output to the unregistered slot on --resume -> fc.ContractError crash. Adds a pure predicate _checkpoint_compatible(checkpoint, ctx) (True when empty or pending writes slot in ctx.registered_slots(), False for a retired/renamed slot) and a discard-and-fresh guard at the top of _run_agent_tick: when the checkpoint is present but incompatible, _clear_checkpoint, record the discard on the tick_start event detail (checkpoint_discarded), and force the FRESH path (resume=False semantics) so the tick re-walks from GUARD and re-pauses with the current migrated writes slot. Applies on BOTH --step and --resume; the fresh re-walk relies on the existing acted-ledger/re-entry idempotency so it never double-acts an open PR. Prior reason: Self-healing known-port adapter-map migration (dogfood REVIEW root-cause fix). A stale persisted project-local adapter-map.json known-port agent entry wired under an older template (e.g. a v0.6.0 REVIEW writing the retired review_verdicts slot with an old output_example) broke the redesigned (FT-C/D) loop where REVIEW writes review_findings. adapter_map_config.migrate_known_port_entries(adapter_map) is a PURE dict->dict transform: for each (port, entry) where ad.is_agent_entry(entry) AND port in AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES it REBUILDS the entry via _build_agent_entry(port, existing dispatch[0].subagent_type), re-deriving writes/cardinality/output_example/inputs/manifest/signal/effect/isolation from the LIVE template while preserving ONLY subagent_type; script strings, custom-port agent entries, and non-agent entries are left unchanged; returns a NEW dict (no input mutation); idempotent. run_tick passes it as the migrate= hook of its single aw.build_loop(...) call (lazily importing adapter_map_config at the call site to avoid the adapter_map_config->run_tick circular import), so a stale entry self-heals on load before resolve+validate every tick.
